accuracy.evidence: Matches EYFS/Y1 cardinality and representation: numeral ↔ exact object count; equal collections share count; digit is a symbol not a countable pile.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets digit-loops-as-count, extras-for-luck, matching by kind/colour/size, and 4-shaped single object in predictions, fix/digit steps, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab builds and repairs representations for a shown numeral — distinct from one-to-one counting procedure (flagcount) and number bonds (flagnbonds).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner must place exact counts, pick matching trays, judge cross-object sameness, fix overfilled trays, and align digit with object count before text confirms.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (shape-as-4; emptiest tray; different because food; draw bigger digit; count loops) are overturned by later build/match/fix tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names shape/loops/curl, luck/safe/more, kind/colour/size, add-the-groups, and ignore/none slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 4–6 wording: short kid lines, counters/apples/cars examples, numeral and count defined in lab prompts.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches cardinality, representation, or a slip to reject.

mobile.evidence: Large add/take and tray buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width.

accessibility.evidence: Build, match, same, fix, digit, and true-idea steps expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK EYFS / National Curriculum Mathematics Y1: Number — count, read and write numerals; represent numbers using objects
NCETM / DfE Mathematics guidance Y1: cardinality and representation with concrete manipulatives
Gelman & Gallistel counting principles (cardinality) as used in early number teaching
